numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Integer-typed bounds overflow/are corrupted when the COPT NLP interface assigns COPT’s float infinity sentinel (stated as 1e30) into an integer bounds array, producing incorrect numerical behavior downstream.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Bounds should be consistently float-typed so that assigning COPT’s 1e30 infinity sentinel does not overflow; i.e., bounds should remain float-typed at the source (use float literals / keep Leaf.get_bounds() float-typed).
trigger_conditions: A variable whose only bound comes from a sign- or boolean-attribute branch that narrows using integer literals, e.g. max(lb_val, 0) and min(ub_val, 1), so lb_val stays an int.
Leaf.get_bounds() then returns np.array(lb_val) as an int64 bounds array.
COPT NLP interface assigns a float infinity sentinel into that integer array when infinite/unbounded bounds are encountered (passage cites 1e30 infinity sentinel).
oracle_clues: The passage explicitly states: “Integer-typed bounds (e.g. from nonneg variables) overflowed when assigning COPT's 1e30 infinity sentinel. Cast bounds to float.”

The passage explains how int typing occurs: “get_bounds() annotates lb_val/ub_val as float, but the sign- and boolean-attribute branches narrowed them with integer literals (max(lb_val, 0), min(ub_val, 1)). For a variable whose only bound comes from such an attribute, lb_val stayed an int and np.array(lb_val) produced an int64 bounds array.”
The fix is described as: “Keep Leaf.get_bounds() bounds float-typed” and “Use float literals so bounds are consistently float-typed at the source.”
The reason COPT can’t handle the infinite values is stated: “we end up with infinite values in the problem we pass COPT. This is both unsupported on their side”.
No concrete numeric input/output triple is provided in the passages (only dtype/typing and sentinel value 1e30 are stated).
